approach: A stateless provider binary reads the frozen initial-input configuration, validates contained authored artifacts with a small generic schema checker, then aggregates opaque external review evidence for the exact checked transition. Versioned configs, templates, and reviewer prompts remain data files.

elements.name: protocol boundary
elements.responsibility: Parse one strict request, dispatch describe or evaluate, and emit one strict result with the defined exit taxonomy.

elements.name: generic schema checker
elements.responsibility: Validate only the allowlisted schema subset and return deterministic exhaustive violations without knowing workflow subjects.

elements.name: evidence evaluator
elements.responsibility: Attribute, conform, supersede, and judge external evidence against configured axes without reading files or judging truth.

elements.name: versioned data profiles
elements.responsibility: Supply policies, schemas, prompts, templates, reviewer protocol, and calibration fixtures outside provider code.

elements.name: speculative plugin registry and cache
elements.responsibility: Register optional future plugins and cache design decisions for reuse across unrelated changes; no current acceptance line requires extensibility or caching.

decisions.choice: Keep revision linkage in a separate config declaration.
decisions.rationale: Cross-artifact equality is needed by this workflow but is not a generic schema keyword.
rejected: Embedding a workflow-specific keyword in the generic checker.

decisions.choice: Use a bounded in-crate schema subset.
decisions.rationale: It provides deterministic shape checks without importing uncalibrated full JSON Schema behavior.
rejected: A full schema dependency with unused keywords.

decisions.choice: Treat author identity as the exact name-kind pair and exclude the subject author.
decisions.rationale: Evidence aggregation needs deterministic distinctness and independence while preserving external claims.
rejected: Cryptographic identity or provider-side author allowlists.

decisions.choice: Add a speculative plugin registry with a config-content cache ahead of any current requirement.
decisions.rationale: Anticipates possible future third-party gate extensions and repeated config reads, accepted as forward investment; no current acceptance line requires it.
rejected: Deferring the registry and cache until an actual extension or performance requirement exists.

risks.risk: An author may edit an artifact materially without changing its declared revision.
risks.mitigation: Trust this residual explicitly and recheck the current declared artifact at every approval boundary.

risks.risk: Manual calibration judgments may reveal a shipped prompt that is too strict.
risks.mitigation: Owner-attested good-but-imperfect fixtures define the futility guard; prompt or config changes bump config_version and restart affected attestation.

risks.risk: The plugin contract may drift before any consumer exists, and the config cache can serve stale policy content after an edit.
risks.mitigation: Version the plugin interface from the start and invalidate the cache on config file modification time.

coverage.acceptance: Frozen obligations and schemas are inspectable before evaluation.
coverage.delivered_by: protocol boundary and versioned data profiles

coverage.acceptance: Malformed artifacts deny before evidence and name every violated rule.
coverage.delivered_by: generic schema checker and exact-transition evaluator

coverage.acceptance: Current evidence must satisfy configured axes and independence rules.
The reference workflow reaches its terminal state only after configured validation obligations are satisfied.
coverage.delivered_by: gate map validation obligations and the terminal transition evaluator
